title: What I Found, In Context: The MOND Acceleration Scale as Dark-Sector Pressure, Its Prior Art, and What Remains Broken
description:
A plain-language orientation piece, written deliberately as an anti-overclaim. It states one idea, the forty-year literature it sits inside, what the idea buys, and what remains broken — including one problem the author cannot currently fix.

THE IDEA. MOND fits galaxy rotation curves with a single dial, an acceleration a_0 ≈ 1.2e-10 m/s^2, whose value has never been derived. Its numerical resemblance to the cosmological acceleration, a_0 ≈ cH_0 ≈ c sqrt(G rho_Lambda), has been noted since the 1980s and has remained a coincidence. Working inside the Aether Scalar Tensor theory of Skordis & Zlosnik (Phys. Rev. Lett. 127, 161302, 2021) — the first relativistic MOND-like theory to pass the cosmic microwave background, and emphatically their result, not the author's — this piece describes setting a_0^2(Q) = kappa^2 G (-K(Q)), identifying the MOND scale with the dark sector's own pressure rather than inserting it by hand.

WHAT FOLLOWS WITHOUT ADJUSTMENT. (1) a_0 ceases to be a free parameter and is fixed by the dark energy density, giving a_0 = kappa c sqrt(G rho_Lambda) = 9.4e-11 m/s^2, with the residual coefficient kappa MEASURED (0.551 +/- 0.043), explicitly NOT derived — four candidate values lie within 2 sigma and the data do not select among them. (2) a_0 is forced to evolve, and it comes out near zero in the early universe and maximal today: 0.6% of its present value at recombination. MOND is therefore switched OFF when the CMB is imprinted, so passing the test that killed the previous generation of these theories becomes a consequence rather than a struggle.

PRIOR ART, STATED PLAINLY. The general move — letting a_0 depend on the dark-sector field so that a_0 evolves — is NOT new. Bekenstein & Sagi (arXiv:0802.1526, 2008) compute exactly this in TeVeS, finding a_0 varying as the exponential of the scalar field; Famaey & McGaugh's Living Review (2012) treats it as established background. What appears specific here is narrower: the identification with the pressure itself rather than with an exponential of the field (so no new function is introduced), the OPPOSITE sign of evolution (rising to a maximum today rather than decreasing), and the setting being AeST rather than TeVeS. The author states explicitly that this is a known idea implemented in a particular way, not a new idea, and that a full priority search has not been completed.

WHAT WORKS: c_T = 1 exactly; a no-ghost theorem; gamma_PPN = 1; a CMB fit computed with CLASS; SPARC rotation curves at 0.108 dex; the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation as a theorem rather than a fit; solar-system dynamics; weak lensing from 40 kpc to 2.2 Mpc.

WHAT DOES NOT WORK, AND IS NOT HIDDEN: galaxy clusters fall short by roughly a factor of two — MOND's forty-year-old open problem, unsolved by TeVeS and by AeST as published. This piece additionally reports why the author's own equation cannot patch it: the available amplitude reduces to the ratio of local dark-sector charge density to dark energy density, and even were that charge the entire dark matter content of the universe the term remains 100 to 1000 times too small. Two further open items are listed rather than omitted: kappa is measured and not derived, and the pressureless component the CMB requires is captured by galaxies and should collapse, with an endpoint in black holes that are not observed.

Every technical claim is backed by a runnable committed script in the accompanying repository, and withdrawn claims — several, including two of the author's own during the week of writing — are recorded there rather than quietly removed.
